question: Who is assigned to ATL-121 and what is its current status?
expected_answer: ATL-121 (Refund workflow implementation) is assigned to Tomas Alvarez and is Blocked.
notes: Single-ticket lookup. Both facts come straight from the ticket fields.

question: Which tickets are overdue?
expected_answer: Six tickets are overdue as of 2026-06-30: ATL-112 (20 days), ATL-109 (15 days), ATL-118 (10 days), ATL-121 (6 days), ATL-127 (4 days), ATL-133 (3 days).
notes: Filter question. Overdue = due_date < 2026-06-30 and status != Done. ATL-116 is due exactly today and must NOT be listed. Done tickets with past due dates must NOT be listed.

question: Why is the checkout card payment screen (ATL-118) late?
expected_answer: ATL-118 is late because the UI is built but cannot submit real payments; it is waiting on the payments API (ATL-112).
notes: Why-question. The reason is in ATL-118's comments, which point to ATL-112. Citing ATL-118 is required; ATL-112 is the root cause and strongly expected.

question: What is blocking Project Atlas?
expected_answer: The payments API v2 delivery (ATL-112) is the root blocker: vendor PayGate has not delivered sandbox credentials (new ETA mid-July). It holds up the checkout card payment screen (ATL-118), refund workflow (ATL-121), end-to-end payment tests (ATL-127), and billing invoice generation (ATL-133).
notes: Multi-ticket synthesis. ATL-112 is REQUIRED (the root cause). The four downstream tickets are for recall: a good answer cites most of them. ATL-109 (privacy policy, waiting on Legal) is overdue but NOT part of the chain; including it as a payments blocker is wrong. ATL-136 (pen test, Blocked) is also unrelated.

question: Why did the due date for load testing of checkout change?
expected_answer: The ATL-124 due date moved from 2026-07-08 to 2026-07-22 because the staging environment upgrade will not finish before 2026-07-15.
notes: Due-date change, explained in an ATL-124 comment. Mentioning ATL-138 (the staging upgrade ticket) is a bonus, not required.

question: When is the Atlas public launch?
expected_answer: The tickets conflict. ATL-103 says public GA is 2026-09-15 (confirmed by the product steering meeting), while ATL-139 says the launch announcement is 2026-10-06 (confirmed by marketing). The data does not say which is authoritative, so the discrepancy should be flagged rather than one date picked.
notes: Contradiction. A correct answer must surface BOTH dates and say they conflict. Confidently giving a single date is a failure.

question: What is the status of the Salesforce CRM integration?
expected_answer: Not found. There is no ticket about a Salesforce CRM integration in the Jira data.
notes: No-data question. Correct behavior is to say it was not found and cite nothing. Inventing a status or citing an unrelated ticket (e.g. ATL-114 inventory sync) is a hallucination.

question: Which tickets are currently Blocked?
expected_answer: Three tickets are Blocked: ATL-112 (Payments API v2 delivery), ATL-121 (Refund workflow implementation), and ATL-136 (Penetration test scheduling).
notes: Status filter. ATL-136 is Blocked but NOT overdue and unrelated to payments (waiting on an external pen-test vendor), which tests that 'blocked' and 'overdue' are not confused.

question: Is the overdue privacy policy ticket late because of the payments API?
expected_answer: No. ATL-109 is overdue because it is waiting on Legal review of the revised data-retention paragraph, not because of the payments API.
notes: Distractor check. ATL-109 is overdue but is not part of the ATL-112 chain; its comment says so explicitly. Agreeing with the premise is a failure.

question: How many days overdue is ATL-112?
expected_answer: ATL-112 is 20 days overdue: it was due 2026-06-10 and today is 2026-06-30.
notes: Tests the frozen TODAY = 2026-06-30. The real system date must never be used.
